8+ years of professional software engineering experience building complex production systems.

Strong software engineering skills in Rust, C/C++, Go, or a comparable system programming language, with the ability to work across the stack, including TypeScript.

Strong understanding of Linux networking internals, with experience building against the kernel networking stack using eBPF/XDP, netlink, and network namespaces.

Experience designing and implementing distributed control planes, desired-state reconciliation, remote configuration, or similar systems that manage large, intermittently connected fleets.

Experience designing secure systems, including threat modeling, least privilege, credential handling, and software supply-chain integrity.

A track record of owning ambiguous initiatives from discovery through production, including architecture, implementation, staged deployment, incident response, and failure analysis.

Technical leadership and communication skills that let you influence decisions, explain system trade-offs to different audiences, and bring stakeholders toward a clear outcome.

Product judgment grounded in customer evidence, usability, and operational simplicity.

Practical experience using AI-assisted engineering tools, coding agents, harnesses, or automation responsibly to improve engineering quality and throughput.

Nice-to-Have Skills

Experience building networking products or systems, such as SD-WAN, SASE, SDN platforms, or network operating systems.

Experience building custom or embedded Linux distributions with immutable, image-based update systems such as RAUC, bootc, or OSTree.

Experience with UEFI Secure Boot, TPMs, hardware-backed identity, or remote attestation.

Experience building networking features such as high-availability failover, dynamic routing, multi-WAN, traffic steering or shaping, application identification, or local policy enforcement.

Experience building automated fleet tests, hardware-in-the-loop or network-in-the-loop test environments, safe staged rollouts, and remote diagnostic tooling.

Professional Experience: 5-8 years building and operating production systems at scale.

Hands-on experience implementing identity protocols or fine-grained authorization systems, RBAC, ABAC, relationship-based access control, or policy engines (such as Cedar), in production.

Language Proficiency: Proficiency in languages like Go and Typescript and comfort working across Cloudflare’s tech stack. 

API Design: Experience designing and building REST APIs: routing, authentication, request lifecycle, and versioning.

Database & Storage: PostgreSQL and Redis experience: schema design, query optimization, caching strategies, and consistency tradeoffs.

High Agency: High standards for correctness and security; curious, self-directed, and comfortable driving ambiguous problems to resolution across team boundaries.

Experience with credential and token lifecycle systems: issuance, rotation, scoping, revocation, or service-to-service authentication at scale.

Familiarity with the Cloudflare developer platform: Workers, Durable Objects, KV, R2, etc.

Experience incrementally re-architecting a large, long-lived codebase under production traffic, and familiarity with containerized deployment (Docker, Kubernetes), infrastructure as code (Terraform), and observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, Kibana).

Experience designing or operating security-sensitive systems, with sound judgment about identity, authorization, credential handling, concurrency, and state management.

Ability to diagnose difficult production issues using logs, metrics, traces, error reporting, and customer-provided evidence, then drive durable fixes.

Experience making backward-compatible changes to live systems and managing the risks of deployment and migration.

Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical tradeoffs, influence decisions across teams, and mentor other engineers.

Austin, US

About the Role

Security at Cloudflare is a focused team committed to helping secure both Cloudflare and our customers. The Threat Detection Automation and Intelligence Team is responsible for identifying, understanding and detecting threats to Cloudflare.

We are seeking an experienced Threat Intelligence Engineer with experience with machine learning data science to join our proactive security team. This role is a critical blend of two disciplines: leveraging Threat Intelligence (TI) to understand the adversary, and then applying advanced Machine Learning and engineering principles to rapidly and effectively defend our organization. The ideal candidate will transform raw threat data into actionable security measures and automated defenses, significantly reducing our mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to respond (MTTR) to sophisticated cyber threats.

Responsibilities

Intelligence Collection & Analysis: Proactively research, collect, and analyze threat intelligence from various sources (OSINT, commercial feeds, dark web, and internal security events) to understand the current and emerging threat landscape.

Machine Learning and Data Science: Design, implement, and maintain detection use cases for the entire machine learning lifecycle (data ingestion, training, deployment, and inference).

Threat Actor Profiling: Develop detailed profiles of relevant threat actors, their Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) using frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK , and identify potential impacts to the organization.

Actionable Intelligence Dissemination: Produce and disseminate timely, relevant, and actionable intelligence reports and briefings for both technical security teams and executive leadership.

IOC/IOA Management: Engineer the ingestion, enrichment, correlation, and contextualization of Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and Indicators of Attack (IOAs) into security platforms.

Automated Defense Development: Design, develop, and implement robust automation workflows and playbooks (SOAR) to streamline security operations tasks, including incident triage, alert enrichment, vulnerability management, and threat response actions.

Tool Integration & Optimization: Integrate diverse security tools (e.g., SIEM, EDR, Cloud Security Posture Management, vulnerability scanners, Threat Intelligence Platforms) through APIs and scripting (primarily Python) to create seamless, automated feedback loops.

Process Improvement: Identify manual, repetitive, and time-consuming security processes and engineer scalable automation solutions to increase team efficiency and operational maturity.

Incident Response Support: Provide threat context  to support the Incident Response team during active security incidents.

Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with Detection Engineers, Security Engineers, and Software Developers to embed security and intelligence-driven practices into the CI/CD pipeline and corporate infrastructure.

Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience

Clear written and verbal communication, and an ability to work through technical decisions with product and engineering partners.

Experience with distributed state, caches, object storage, or safe migration of a legacy production service.

Role Summary

Back in 2014, Cloudflare launched Universal SSL to provide all of our customers with the security of encrypted traffic between visitors and Cloudflare’s network. On the day we flipped the switch, we doubled the amount of sites using SSL/TLS on the internet. Since then, we’ve been working on providing even more ways to encrypt traffic easier and more effectively. To better serve our customers, we’re constantly improving our systems for issuing, managing, and deploying TLS certificates. We’re continuously providing technology to site owners that was previously only available to the largest organizations. Your contributions will help make the web a faster, safer, better, and more heavily encrypted place.

You will design and implement alerts, write procedures for ops to handle such alerts, or serve as an escalation point for unresolved operational issues. Familiarity with PKI/TLS concepts and certificate management

Experience working with law enforcement and legal requests for customer information.

Deep technical experience understanding how the Internet works. 

Understanding of the Internet ecosystem and the roles and functions of the various types of online service providers.

title: Academy Professor, French & Portuguese
description:
Role Summary

HubSpot Academy is on a mission to be the place people go to learn how to start and grow a business. We offer a variety of educational and inspirational content — from lessons and full certification courses to live, hands-on workshops — that provides valuable business training to people all over the world. This educational content generates new customers for the business and delights our existing ones in service of achieving their business and career goals.

We're looking for a Professional HubSpot Academy Professor - Coach who is passionate about helping customers confidently use HubSpot tools through live, hands-on small group coaching sessions. This role is ideal for someone who shows growing independence and proficiency in live facilitation and content creation, effectively applying skills to enhance customer outcomes while contributing to HubSpot's educational mission at scale.

As a Professional HubSpot Academy Professor - Coach at HubSpot Academy, you'll be responsible for developing and delivering live, small group coaching sessions focused on specific HubSpot tools and use cases, as well as creating supporting on-demand educational content. You'll design engaging workshop experiences and practical learning resources that solve real customer problems, drive product adoption, and support long-term usage of HubSpot products. The role requires good understanding of adult learning principles, live facilitation skills, content creation abilities, and comprehensive knowledge of HubSpot's product offerings, as well as a passion for crafting hands-on learning experiences that deliver measurable impact at scale.

This role sits on the HubSpot Academy team and reports to the Manager of HubSpot Academy Education. You'll work alongside other Academy Professors and Customer Evangelists to develop comprehensive educational strategies that align with HubSpot's business objectives and support customers at scale.

What you'll do:

Facilitate High-Impact Small Group Coaching Sessions:

Lead multiple live, interactive coaching sessions each week for groups of customers focused on specific HubSpot tools, features, or use cases (e.g., Advanced CRM, Marketing Automation, Customer Agent, Loop Marketing plays)

Run sessions in alignment with standardized agendas and learning objectives while adapting to the needs and questions of each cohort in real-time

Demonstrate growing expertise in facilitating workshops where customers work on their real HubSpot challenges and leave having configured something concrete in their portal

Create supportive learning environments where customers feel comfortable asking questions, sharing use cases, and learning from peers

Create Supporting On-Demand Content:

Develop short educational videos, workbooks, and guides that complement small group coaching topics and enable customers to review key concepts

Create practical resources that customers can reference when implementing what they learned during coaching sessions

Design follow-up materials that reinforce session learning and support continued product adoption

Collaborate with Instructional Designers and content creators to ensure cohesive learning experiences across live and on-demand formats

Drive Product Adoption and Usage Uplift:

Design sessions and supporting content so customers leave with actionable next steps and concrete configurations in their HubSpot portals

Partner cross-functionality to understand which specific actions and sessions drive the largest usage movement

Refine content and facilitation approaches based on data showing what drives measurable customer outcomes

Track how coaching sessions contribute to customer activation, feature adoption, and ongoing product usage

Collaborate Cross-Functionally:

Work closely with Academy, Product, Creative, and Marketing teams to align session topics with product launches, spotlight moments, and strategic initiatives (e.g., AI adoption, Loop Marketing, Customer Agent)

Provide structured feedback to Product and leadership on what customers are saying and where they're getting stuck

Ensure coaching insights inform product roadmap and enablement priorities

Participate in cross-functional projects to develop educational strategies aligned with business goals

Maintain Operational Excellence:

Ensure accurate logging of sessions and attendance via Bevy and HubSpot systems, partnering with operations teams to resolve data integrity issues

Follow established workflows for customer inquiries about registration, scheduling, or follow-up questions

Use tools like Asana, AirTable, and Google Suite to coordinate session planning, content development, and track key metrics

Monitor registration and attendance patterns to optimize session timing, topics, and promotional approaches

Continuously Improve Content and Experience:

Iterate on session content, flow, and activities based on NPS, CSAT, qualitative feedback, and performance metrics (attendance, usage impact, repeat attendance)

Collect session feedback to continuously improve both live facilitation and supporting on-demand content

Experiment with new formats (e.g., "Build With" sessions, customer guest speakers, region-specific variants)

Share insights with the broader team to enhance the small group coaching program and on-demand content library

What you'll bring:

Required Qualifications

Fluency in French and Portuguese

You have demonstrated experience leading live trainings, workshops, or group sessions (virtual or in-person) where you taught, demoed, and troubleshooted on the fly.

You possess exceptional facilitation and communication skills—you can read a room, simplify complex topics, and keep diverse audiences engaged and on track.

You have strong product aptitude and quickly learn new features, connecting them to real-world customer use cases across Marketing, Sales, and Service workflows.

You effectively communicate and collaborate with customers and cross-functional teams to align on coaching objectives and customer needs.

You're energized by scale—reaching hundreds or thousands of customers through repeatable experiences—and see group coaching as core to the future of customer education.

You're customer-obsessed and empathetic, able to meet customers where they are in their journey, even when they're just beginning with advanced features.

You comfortably adjust to changing priorities in a fast-evolving environment where programs, tools, and processes are being optimized, and you actively contribute to improvements.

You can craft well-structured written content for workbooks, guides, and supporting materials that enhance learning experiences.

You independently explore and suggest innovative approaches to coaching and content creation, experimenting with new facilitation techniques and formats.

Nice to Have:

Experience working directly with HubSpot (as a user, partner, or prior HubSpotter), especially across multiple Hubs

Experience facilitating global customer audiences across time zones

Familiarity with event platforms, and/or prior experience in scaled programs or live onboarding

Experience creating short-form video content or educational materials

title: Business Development Representative - DACH
description:
Standort: Remote in Deutschland oder flexibles Büro in Berlin

Wir bei HubSpot laden alle, unabhängig vom Abschluss, ein, sich unserem Vertriebsteam als Business Development Representative (kurz BDR) anzuschließen. Unser Ziel ist es, eine vielfältige und inklusive Arbeitsumgebung zu schaffen, die Talente verschiedener Generationen schätzt und fördert. Ob du gerade deine Ausbildung abgeschlossen hast oder deine Karriere im SaaS-Vertrieb beschleunigen möchtest, wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung. Gemäß Modells für die Zukunft der Arbeit bieten wir sowohl Büro- als auch Remote-Arbeitsmöglichkeiten innerhalb Deutschlands an.  

Die Aufgabe eines Business Development Representative besteht darin, durch strategische Kundengewinnung geeignete Unternehmen zu identifizieren und mit diesen zu interagieren. Dies geschieht unter Verwendung bereits existierender HubSpot-Leads, deren Interesse durch Anrufe, E-Mails sowie Messaging über soziale Medien erneut geweckt wird.

Im Rahmen deiner Kontaktaufnahme mit potenzieller Kundschaft erfährst du als BDR mehr darüber, mit welchen Herausforderungen sich das jeweilige Unternehmen konfrontiert sieht, und können so entscheiden, ob HubSpot hier als Lösung herangezogen werden kann. Wenn du einen qualifizierten Interessenten oder eine qualifizierte Interessentin identifiziert hast, besteht Ihr Ziel darin, den Wert von HubSpot prägnant und präzise zu kommunizieren und Interesse an einem tiefer gehenden Gespräch mit einem Account Executive zu wecken.

Dein Verantwortungsbereich umfasst die enge Zusammenarbeit mit 2 bis 3 Account Executives. Du wirst täglich mit den von dir unterstützten Account Executives sowie mit anderen BDRs zusammenarbeiten, um innovative Strategien zur Ermittlung neuer Opportunität zu entwickeln. BDRs, die sich erfolgreich in ihrer Rolle behaupten, werden anschließend zu Account Executives innerhalb unseres Vertriebsteams.

Was fällt in den Verantwortungsbereich eines Business Development Representative?

Folgende Aufgaben und Verantwortungen erwarten dich in dieser Vollzeitsbeschäftigung: 

Ein hoher Umfang an Outbound-Aktivitäten zur Akquise und Qualifizierung von Leads (neue Kunden)

Eng mit Account Executives zusammenarbeiten, um Strategien und Pläne für die Kundengewinnung zu entwickeln und zu implementieren

Planen von Online-Produktdemonstrationen für qualifizierte Leads bei gleichzeitigem Sicherstellen, dass deine monatlichen Ziele erreicht werden

Verstehen der Bedürfnisse und Herausforderungen von Kunden und Kundinnen unter Einsatz bestimmter Verkaufsmethoden wie der BANT-Methodik

Durchführen von Marktforschung, um den Kundenstamm von HubSpot zu erweitern

Welche Voraussetzungen gibt es für diese Stelle?

Engagement und Begeisterung für die Technologiebranche und den Vertrieb

Arbeitserfahrung im Bereich Vertrieb oder Kundengewinnung und in einer wachstumsstarken „Scale-up“-Umgebung ist nicht erforderlich, aber von Vorteil

Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse

Scharfer, zielorientierter Fokus und ein überzeugender, stringenter Ansatz bei der Zielumsetzung

Die Fähigkeit, mit Einwänden umzugehen und auf diese einzugehen, sowie die Bereitschaft, sich coachen zu lassen

Starke Organisationsfähigkeit und sehr gutes Zeitmanagement

Leidenschaft dafür, Unternehmen bei ihrem Wachstum zu unterstützen, und Interesse für die Technologiebranche

Was hast du davon?

Ein hybrides Arbeitsmodell, das persönliche Arbeitspräferenzen berücksichtigt

Tolle Teammitglieder in einem kulturell vielfältigen Arbeitsumfeld sowie Unterstützung durch eine Mentorin oder einen Mentor

Interaktives Mitarbeitertraining und ein einmonatiges Onboarding, um dir den Einstieg zu erleichtern

Ein klar abgesteckter Karriereweg mit regelmäßigen Aufstiegsmöglichkeiten

Erstattung von Studiengebühren in Höhe von maximal 4.250 Euro im Jahr und ein kostenloses Bücherprogramm, um die persönliche Weiterbildung zu fördern 

Coaching- und Therapiesitzungen über die Modern Health-App zur Förderung des mentalen Wohlbefindens sowie andere Gesundheitsleistungen, z. B. Lebensversicherung, Absicherungen im Falle längerer Krankheit oder Erstattung von Fitnessstudiogebühren in Höhe von bis zu 250 Euro

title: Lead Corporate Account Executive - France
description:
HubSpot : Philosophie et Produit

Nous pensons que le monde a changé. Nous constatons que les entreprises utilisent davantage de types de logiciels — et non moins — qui doivent tous fonctionner ensemble. Pour aider nos clients à mieux croître dans cet environnement, HubSpot évolue d’une suite « tout-en-un » vers une plateforme « tout-sur-un ».

HubSpot est un ensemble d’outils qui soutient les équipes en contact avec les clients, notamment le Marketing, les Ventes et le Service, afin de les aider à optimiser chaque étape du parcours d’achat et à développer leur activité.

La philosophie du flywheel de HubSpot utilise l’élan des clients satisfaits pour générer des recommandations et des ventes récurrentes pour nos clients. Nous avons également investi dans un écosystème d’intégrations qui permet aux clients d’en faire davantage avec HubSpot et crée une véritable valeur pour les personnes qui adoptent notre suite logicielle.

Nous recrutons activement un·e Lead Corporate Account Executive ; les candidat·e·s peuvent travailler au bureau, en mode hybride ou à distance depuis la France selon leur préférence ! Veuillez consulter cet article pour davantage de contexte : The Future of Work at HubSpot: How We're Building a Hybrid Company.

Votre rôle chez HubSpot

En tant que Lead Corporate Account Executive chez HubSpot, vous interviendrez directement auprès d’entreprises de taille moyenne à grande et les aiderez à croître. Vous utiliserez des stratégies de vente proactives  pour trouver et conclure de nouvelles opportunités, tout en augmentant l’usage de la plateforme HubSpot par vos clients au fil du temps. Vous utiliserez votre connaissance de la transformation digitale et du change management pour agir comme un conseiller de confiance auprès du client, en gérant l’ensemble du processus de vente avec lui.

Quelles sont les responsabilités d’un·e Corporate Account Executive ?

Développer et être responsable de votre propre plan d’affaires annuel, trimestriel et mensuel pour votre territoire.

Trouver de nouveaux prospects

title: Lead Data Analyst
description:
POS-28273

Company Overview

At HubSpot, we aim to help businesses grow better every day. We strive to have a high-performing team developing sales strategies that align with our mission to empower growth through strategic partnerships with sales leaders.

Team & Segment Overview

The EMEA Upmarket Sales Strategy team acts as trusted, strategic partners to the EMEA Upmarket Sales leaders, enabling them to make data-backed decisions that increase productivity and drive revenue growth. 

Job Summary

As a Lead Sales Strategy Analyst for EMEA Upmarket, you will be a primary driver and owner of analytics, models, and business frameworks and processes that guide & facilitate the EMEA Upmarket segment to run its business. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy to define the right questions, build decision-ready insights, and influence Director and VP-level decisions on strategy, capacity, and investment for one of HubSpot’s most important segments.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic analytics partner - Diagnosing performance, defining KPIs, and translating data into clear "what / so what / now what" narratives for Sales Directors and VPs to support business decisions.

Reporting - Building and owning core reporting assets (scorecards, pipeline dashboards, capacity views) in Looker, Hex, SQL, and Sheets - ensuring accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder self-serve.

Processes - Designing and leading core business processes. Defining inputs, building integrated views, and surfacing risk and upside in actionable form - across core areas such as forecasting, headcount, capacity, and territory planning.

Project Management - Acting as DRI on critical cross-functional projects and coordinating across Sales Strategy, Ops, Finance & other stakeholders. Aligning teams around a shared view of data, problems, and priorities and being prepared to influence without authority. 

Coaching - Supporting the development of other analysts, and creating reusable templates, metric definitions, and documentation that scale the function beyond individual contributions.

Qualifications

Typically 5+ years of experience in sales strategy, sales operations, business analytics, management consulting, or a related analytical role, with meaningful ownership of a segment, region, or business line.

Demonstrated ability to define and solve complex business problems, from framing and hypothesis setting through analysis, recommendation, and follow-through.

Strong analytical toolkit, including:

Proficiency with BI and analytics tools (e.g., Looker, Hex, Tableau, or similar).

Advanced skills in Google Sheets / Excel for analysis and modeling.

Working proficiency querying and transforming large datasets.

Proven AI fluency: demonstrated ability to use AI tools, such as Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude, to analyze data and automate processes.

Proven SQL knowledge and experience.

Proven experience owning core models and reporting for a business area and using them to drive decisions with senior stakeholders.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of influencing Director- and VP-level leaders using clear narratives, visuals, and frameworks.

Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, autonomous working environment. 

Strong capability to identify personal and professional growth opportunities and willingness to expand beyond baseline responsibilities.

title: Manager, Analytics Engineering, Data & AI Foundations
description:
POS-33330

Manager, Analytics Engineering, Data & AI Foundations

HubSpot's mission is to Help Millions of Organizations Grow Better. HubSpot's Operations team is core to this goal by supporting the HubSpotters who drive growth and serve HubSpot's customers. Our goal in Operations is to embed advanced analytics and algorithmic intelligence into the DNA of decision-making across HubSpot. Flexible, well connected, well architected data are the backbone of our strategy, along with the Analytics Engineers who create that landscape.

In this role, you'll join the Data & AI Foundations team and lead Analytics Engineers responsible for the shared data foundations, platform capabilities, and AI enabled workflows that make HubSpot's Analytics Engineering organization more effective and scalable. You'll work across Analytics Engineering managers, analysts, analytics committees, and technical platform partners to understand workflows, identify friction, and turn feedback into a clear strategy and prioritized roadmap. You'll combine people leadership, technical judgment, change management, and hands on problem solving to help the organization adopt new ways of working.

In this role, you'll get to:

Lead and develop a team of Analytics Engineers, supporting career growth, hiring and retention, regular feedback, and alignment to the highest-impact priorities

Set the team's vision and operating model, translating broader Operations and Analytics Engineering goals into a focused roadmap and clear measures of success

Partner with Analytics Engineering managers to understand team workflows and identify opportunities to improve composable agents, semantic models, shared data assets, and developer tooling

Collaborate with analysts and analytics committees that use shared Analytics Engineering assets or build their own agents, incorporating their feedback into platform strategy and delivery

Work with technical leaders to review architecture and implementation approaches, establish scalable standards, and ensure solutions are robust, practical, and reusable

Prioritize a portfolio of cross functional initiatives, defining objectives, sequencing, responsibilities, and resource allocation based on impact and team capacity

Partner with AI Readiness delivery teams to deploy implementation resources against the highest priority work and remove blockers through execution

Own and evolve core platform assets, Analytics Engineering tooling, reusable patterns, and automation that raise the floor for every Analytics Engineer

Advance our composable agentic Analytics Engineering delivery system and support responsible adoption of AI-assisted workflows across the organization

Guide the development of semantic models and metric layers that serve as trusted, reusable foundations for analytics and AI consumption

Establish and champion standards for data modeling, testing, code review, documentation, observability, reliability, and cost management

Build enablement programs and cross-functional partnerships that help teams adopt modern tools and practices, while staying close enough to the work to contribute hands-on when it will accelerate progress

We are looking for someone with:

Experience leading and developing Analytics Engineers or similar technical data professionals, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and career development

Demonstrated ability to help define a vision and translate it into a practical strategy, roadmap, and operating model

Strong understanding of analysts' workflows and the role of shared data assets, tooling, and standards in improving quality and scale

Strong proficiency with SQL, data modeling, ETL, ELT, and modern data tools such as Snowflake, dbt, and Looker

Hands-on dbt experience, including scalable modeling patterns, testing, macros, and development workflows

Experience building or managing shared data platform assets, developer toolkits, internal frameworks, semantic models, or metric layers

Experience with AI assisted development and agentic workflows, such as Claude Code, composable skill based systems, AI agents, or MCP integrations

A track record of leading complex, cross-functional data initiatives from an ambiguous problem through production

Experience driving change and adoption across a large or complex organization, including influencing without direct authority and building accountability across teams

Strong prioritization and project management skills, including defining success criteria, sequencing work, and balancing impact with team capacity

A DevOps mindset characterized by automation, collaboration, continuous improvement, reliability, and frequent iteration based on user needs

Strong communication skills and the ability to distill technical decisions, trade-offs, and strategy into clear business terms

Experience working with globally distributed teams and version control tools such as GitHub Enterprise Cloud

Experience with Python is a plus, but not required

title: Outbound Business Development Representative (BDR)
description:
🚀 Join HubSpot as an Outbound Business Development Representative (BDR)
 📍 Remote (USA) or Cambridge, MA, USA

We’ll be honest — sales isn’t easy, and it’s not for everyone. But for those who love a challenge, thrive on results, and want to launch a long-term path in sales, it’s incredibly rewarding.

If you’re looking to “try out” sales or just dip a toe in, this probably isn’t the role for you. But, if you’re the kind of person who wakes up hungry to compete, thrives on setting and smashing goals, and wants to build a career in tech sales from the ground up — we want to talk to you.

At HubSpot, our BDRs are not only the first point of contact for our prospects—they’re also developing the skills and mindset to become our next generation of Account Executives. This is not a placeholder job — it’s the first chapter of a high-growth sales career designed for those who want to build skills, embrace feedback, move fast, and grow even faster.

The Role:
As an Outbound BDR, you’ll play a key role in HubSpot’s growth engine. You'll be the first touchpoint for many of our future customers, sparking conversations through strategic outreach, uncovering pain points, and qualifying leads. You’ll partner closely with Account Executives to deliver high-quality meetings that drive pipeline, impact, and revenue. HubSpot is an all-in-one marketing, sales, and service software platform that helps businesses grow and succeed. title: Principal Software Engineer
description:
About the Team

HubSpot's Adaptive Monetization group owns the systems that determine how customers buy, contract, and pay for HubSpot — at scale, with direct financial consequence. Our infrastructure handles usage metering, contract orchestration, and subscription lifecycle management for every customer on the platform. An outage here doesn't just affect user experience; it blocks customers from purchasing HubSpot entirely, and bugs typically produce immediate, measurable financial impact.

We're in the middle of a multi-year shift to transform HubSpot's straight-line SaaS subscription model and replace it with a flexible contracting layer that can support usage-based billing, commit-based pricing, and enterprise-grade contract structures. This work has executive visibility and is directly tied to HubSpot's revenue growth and ships meaningful impact to our customers.

The core team for this role is roughly 15 engineers across 3 focused team, with an additional influence and impact radius that extends across approximately 180 engineers in the broader Fintech organization.

About the Role

We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to help architect, build, and influence the evolution of HubSpot’s monetization model and strategy — and to do it incrementally, on a system that is live and load-bearing every day.

This is a hands-on technical role. Approximately 70-80% of your time will be spent writing code, leading designs, reviewing architectures, and owning technical direction on some of the most complex systems at HubSpot. The remainder will be split between cross-functional strategy, mentoring, and building technical credibility across the broader fintech engineering organization.

This is not a greenfield opportunity. The ideal person is someone who finds genuine satisfaction in making a complex, mission-critical legacy system incrementally better — and who can bring others along on that journey. If you've thrived at a publicly traded fintech company navigating the intersection of audit rigor, product velocity, and distributed systems complexity, this role was written for you.

What You'll Do

Architect the future of HubSpot's contract and monetization layer

Lead the technical strategy for moving HubSpot from a fixed SaaS subscription model to a flexible contracting platform that supports usage-based, commit-based, and enterprise-grade pricing structures.

Define and own the core architecture for contract lifecycle management, usage metering, entitlement enforcement, and pricing model extensibility — using our internal Corex contract orchestration framework as the foundation.

Make principled tradeoffs between correctness, compliance, and product velocity in a system where the stakes are financial.

Be a deeply hands-on, high-leverage builder

Write production code regularly. Lead design reviews. Own large initiatives end-to-end, from architecture through rollout.

Drive multi-team technical efforts that span the three squads within Adaptive Monetization and require coordination across the broader fintech organization.

Turn ambiguity into clear technical direction and working software — and stay hands-on throughout.

Navigate complexity without creating it

Incrementally improve systems that cannot be rewritten from scratch. HubSpot's current contract infrastructure is load-bearing; this work requires surgical precision, not clean-slate thinking.

Bring the team with you — identifying paths forward that are safe to ship incrementally while maintaining reliability.

Raise the bar on resilience and observability in a system that generates dozens of production pages per day as the business shifts toward new pricing models.

Communicate with clarity across the organization

Translate deeply technical architectural decisions for finance, compliance, legal, and executive stakeholders. This role requires you to operate effectively in rooms where the other people are not engineers.

Influence the product roadmap by helping leadership understand technical tradeoffs between speed, correctness, and long-term platform health.

Represent the engineering perspective on pricing strategy, contract flexibility, and go-to-market changes that require systems changes to support.

Grow the fintech engineering organization

Mentor senior and staff engineers within Adaptive Monetization and across the broader Fintech org.

Partner with your peers — including the other Fintech principal engineers — to align on patterns that reduce complexity and increase reliability across the organization.

Participate in recruiting and help raise the hiring bar for technical talent in the fintech space.

What You Bring

Proven experience designing and evolving distributed systems with strict financial correctness requirements — billing infrastructure, payment processing, contract management, usage metering, or similar.

A background at a publicly traded company where audit rigor, compliance constraints, and real-money consequences shaped the way you built software. Engineers from Stripe, Block, Adyen, PayPal, or similar environments tend to arrive with the right instincts for this work.

The ability to operate effectively on complex, legacy systems that cannot be paused or rewritten — you know how to make progress incrementally while protecting reliability.

Strong executive communication skills. You can walk a CFO or compliance officer through a technical architecture decision, adapt the framing to what they care about, and leave the room with alignment.

A mentorship orientation. You're someone junior engineers seek out, and you measure your impact in part by how much better the engineers around you get.

Comfort with ambiguity. The system this role is responsible for is changing faster than it was designed to handle. You'll receive a lot of signal and need to make good decisions quickly.

Deep backend engineering expertise. This is not a platform, DevEx, or infrastructure role — the work is in the financial logic, data models, and service contracts that power HubSpot's monetization.

Why This Role Matters

HubSpot's ability to offer commit-based enterprise contracts, charge based on usage, and compete for the largest, most complex customers in the market depends entirely on the contracting and monetization infrastructure this role will help build. This is multi-year work with direct revenue consequence and executive visibility — and the person who leads the technical architecture of this system will have a meaningful impact on what HubSpot can sell, and to whom, for years to come.

title: Principal Software Engineer
description:
POS-5690

About the Team

The Observability team owns the internal platform that gives every HubSpot engineer real visibility into how their systems behave in production. We build and operate the distributed tracing, metrics, alerting, and logging infrastructure that spans hundreds of microservices, billions of daily events, and thousands of engineers who depend on that signal to ship reliably.

We are now investing in the next generation of this platform. As HubSpot deploys AI agents and ML-powered features across the product, the team is building the tracing and telemetry primitives that make it possible to understand, debug, and trust what those systems are doing in production. This is greenfield, technically interesting work at a scale few companies operate at and we are looking for a Principal Engineer to help lead it.

About the Role

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to be the technical anchor for HubSpot’s Observability platform. This role sits at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, developer platform design, and AI observability. A big part of this role is working horizontally across a large engineering org and setting patterns and standards that make it easier for teams to instrument, alert on, and reason about their services. You will also shape how we trace and understand our growing fleet of AI agents and ML systems in production: a technically distinct and increasingly critical problem.

Key Expectations

Observability Platform Architecture: Define the patterns and evolution of HubSpot’s core telemetry platform — distributed tracing, metrics, and structured logging — at a scale that spans hundreds of services and billions of daily events. Set the standards for how instrumentation is done across a large, polyglot engineering organization.

AI & Agentic Observability: Lead the technical strategy for tracing and understanding AI agents and ML-powered systems in production. Define the primitives, telemetry standards, and debugging workflows that help product engineers understand what their models and agents are doing — and build trust in those systems over time. This is greenfield and consequential work.

High-Cardinality, High-Throughput Systems: Architect telemetry pipelines and storage systems that handle high-cardinality data at high throughput without blowing up cost or query latency. Make principled tradeoffs between sampling, fidelity, retention, and developer ergonomics.

Hands-on, High-Leverage Builder: Ship production code. Lead design reviews and take high-impact initiatives end-to-end, from prototype to production system at scale. Stay close to the systems you build and be the person who can debug the hardest problems when they surface.

Developer Experience & Adoption: Design the instrumentation APIs and libraries that product engineers reach for, making correct observability the path of least resistance. Drive OpenTelemetry adoption across a large, polyglot codebase. Build the tooling that turns raw telemetry into actionable signal for teams operating at speed.

Production Intelligence & Reliability Patterns: Define patterns for SLO/SLI design, alerting philosophy, and how teams graduate from reactive to proactive incident response. Push for simplicity in a domain that wants to get complicated, and consistency where tooling can drift across a large organization.

Technical Leadership & Influence: Partner with infrastructure, platform, and product engineering teams to understand their signal gaps and close them. Influence technical strategy alongside engineering leadership, translating observability constraints and opportunities into product and operational decisions. Mentor senior engineers and tech leads, driving thoughtful design decisions and capturing learnings from major incidents and large-scale migrations.

What You Bring

Platform-Builder Experience: Proven experience building observability or telemetry tooling for internal engineering teams, rather than simply consuming it. You understand how to architect developer platforms that serve thousands of engineers across a large organization, backed by deep operational instincts and hard-earned expertise.

Telemetry Systems Depth: Deep expertise navigating trade-offs in telemetry pipeline design across high-cardinality data, dynamic sampling, query latency, retention economics, and data fidelity. Strong technical fluency with OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing engines, metric backends, and large-scale log ingestion infrastructure.

Incident Automation & Operational Excellence: Proven track record linking telemetry signals directly to automated operational workflows. You have designed architecture for real-time telemetry triggers that power automated remediation, dynamic runbooks, or AI-assisted root-cause diagnosis across microservices environments.

Why This Role, Why Now

HubSpot is scaling fast — more engineers, more microservices, more AI systems running in production — and the Observability platform is at an inflection point. The foundations are solid, but the next phase requires a different kind of investment: rethinking cardinality economics, making OpenTelemetry the default across a large polyglot org, and building an entirely new layer of AI tracing that doesn’t yet exist.

This Principal Engineer will have a direct line of sight from the architecture they design to the engineering outcomes we measure: incident response times, adoption rates, developer satisfaction, and the trust that product teams place in their production signal. The AI observability layer in particular is greenfield — there is no playbook to follow, which is exactly what makes this the right moment for the right person.

If you want to build the platform that helps thousands of engineers understand what their systems are doing — including systems powered by AI that are genuinely hard to see inside — this is the role.

description:
POS-33518

 About the Team

Breeze Assistant is HubSpot's AI-powered gateway to value — the conversational front door through which every HubSpot customer starts their work, gets outcomes, and grows with the product. Our mission is to make Breeze the fastest, best way to achieve sales and marketing outcomes in HubSpot: from a new customer's very first session through the seasoned marketer orchestrating complex multi-step GTM workflows.

We significantly increased both CSAT and weekly active penetration by building a foundation-first, tightly-scoped system. We are now running that same playbook at scale — shipping a full agentic platform that every HubSpot team builds on. The next leg of the journey is larger: Breeze becomes the place a customer can get any GTM task done, powered by complete customer context, agentic everboarding, and a platform mature enough that partners and internal teams build their most important use cases on top of it.

If a marketer or seller can get their real work done — and done better — inside Breeze, they stay in HubSpot, come back, and grow. We build so they never have to leave.

About the Role

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to be the technical anchor for the Breeze Assistant platform. This role sits at the intersection of robust distributed systems, bleeding-edge Generative AI, and real customer outcomes.

You are not just following a roadmap — you are helping define it. You will shape how Breeze moves from a highly capable assistant to a trusted, proactive agent: one that delivers durable, shareable artifacts grounded in CRM data; dynamically generates the UI a user needs for the task at hand; orchestrates multi-step workflows across HubSpot and third-party tools; and learns from every interaction to get better. The scale is real — millions of users, petabytes of context, and a platform that every HubSpot engineering team depends on.

Key Expectations

Agentic Platform Architecture: Define the patterns for how AI agents safely interact with HubSpot's CRM, agentic primitives (skills, tools, memory, scheduled prompts), and third-party ecosystems (Slack, Google Workspace, Gong, etc.). You set the bar for how Breeze orchestrates deterministic and non-deterministic steps — choosing the right blend for trust, cost, and outcome quality.

Building Breakthrough Surfaces: Breeze already delivers a significant volume of artifacts across reports, decks, and pages. You will extend the platform so every HubSpot team builds their highest-value deliverables into Breeze — expanding artifact types, opening the platform for internal builders, and driving toward Breeze being the default surface for customers and teams to build on.

Complete Customer Context: Work closely with the Context team to ensure every Breeze interaction is powered by complete, trustworthy growth context: company and industry data, outcome history, learning loops, and customer goals. You will build the technical bridges that let context evolve from a data layer into a dynamic, active collaborator in every user's GTM work.

Rapid GenAI Experimentation: Act as a zero-to-one builder. You stay current with the latest in LLMs, RAG, and agentic frameworks  to rapidly prototype and validate new capabilities — and you know when to ship the prototype and when to wait for production-grade infrastructure.

Hands-on, High-Leverage Contributor: You ship production code. You will lead development of high-impact initiatives, moving from a prototype to a production system supporting a broad user base.

System Reliability & Trust: Ensure GenAI outputs are not just capable, but trustworthy. You will drive strategy around LLM evaluation, observability, guardrails, and data privacy — the technical foundation that lets customers trust Breeze enough to run real business processes on it.

Cross-Functional Technical Leadership: Breeze is both a product and a platform. You will partner with Product, AI Research, HubSpot engineering teams, and the Ecosystem teams to ensure every HubSpot team can expose their tools and API endpoints to Breeze — because coverage is the single biggest unlock for use-case completeness.

Technical Mentorship & Multiplier: Elevate AI fluency across the engineering org. Mentor senior engineers on prompt engineering, model selection, agentic design patterns, and the nuances of building non-deterministic systems at scale.

What You Bring

Proven Expertise in Distributed Systems: You have built and scaled high-throughput, low-latency systems with strict reliability requirements — the kind that support high concurrency and vast data scale.

GenAI Proficiency: Deep experience with LLM orchestration, vector databases, RAG pipelines, and multi-agent frameworks. You understand the trade-offs between model architectures, fine-tuning strategies, and inference costs, and you make principled bets.

Agentic System Design: A background in building autonomous or semi-autonomous systems where AI takes actions, handles tool-calling, manages complex state, and recovers gracefully from failure. You've thought hard about the interplay between deterministic and non-deterministic steps in production workflows.

Platform Thinking: You build for other builders. You design primitives — skills, tools, APIs, agentic harnesses — that internal teams and partners can compose into use cases you haven't imagined yet.

User-First Mindset: You have a track record of building products that people love. You advocate for the end-user in design reviews and understand the pain points of sales and marketing professionals well enough to know when a technical tradeoff harms the outcome.

Bias for Action: You prefer a working prototype over a lengthy design doc. You turn ambiguity into clear plans and working software, and you know how to balance the speed of AI experimentation with the rigor of production-grade systems.

Rapid Domain Fluency: The AI landscape changes weekly. You dive into a new paper, model, or framework today and can explain its strategic value — and its limitations — to the team tomorrow.

Why This Role, Why Now

Breeze is at an inflection point. The foundation works — CSAT and WAU are both climbing, artifacts are resonating, and the agentic platform is coming online. The next phase is about scale, coverage, and trust: making Breeze the place where every HubSpot customer does their most important work, on a platform mature enough that every Hub team builds their highest-value customer journeys into it.

This Principal Engineer will have a direct line of sight from the architecture they design to the customer outcomes we measure — WAU, CSAT, artifacts opened, credits consumed. If you want to build AI systems that matter at scale, with a team that has already proven the playbook works, this is the role.

description:

Principal Software Engineer-  CRM Product Platform

Engineering | Remote - USA 

About the Team

HubSpot's Product Platform Engineering org is building the foundational layer that powers how millions of users experience, configure, and get value from the CRM. We own the shared infrastructure, APIs, extensibility surfaces, and product foundations that run across every Hub-  not one feature team, but all of them. When we ship, it shows up everywhere.

We operate as a product-line triad with Product Management and UX- which means tight, fast collaboration from problem discovery through production delivery. The org is in one of its most formative periods: we're redefining how customers interact with and configure HubSpot at a moment when AI is fundamentally changing what's possible in SaaS products. Engineers here don't just execute a roadmap - they help set one.

About the Role

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to lead one of the most compelling product challenges in the CRM space right now: making HubSpot deeply, genuinely configurable for every customer-  without sacrificing the reliability and consistency enterprise software demands.

The shift is already happening. Things that once required expensive custom engineering - personalizing workflows, building bespoke CRM applications, extending the product to fit a team's exact needs -  are becoming dramatically more accessible with coding agents and AI. The question we're solving is: how do you productize that level of deep customization at scale? This person won't just follow a technical roadmap-  they'll help define what's possible, build the custom workspaces and extensibility foundations that make it real, and raise the bar for how product-minded engineering gets done across a 100+ engineer org.

Key Expectations

Architectural Leadership for CRM Configurability: Define the technical patterns for how customers can deeply configure and extend HubSpot-  from custom workspaces and no-code/low-code surfaces to AI-powered personalization that scales across millions of users.

Zero-to-One Product Building: Act as the technical anchor for a genuinely new problem space. You stay current with where AI and coding agents are heading, prototype rapidly, and turn early-stage ideas into production-grade product features-  not just POCs.

Hands-On, High-Leverage Contributor: You ship production code at 75%+ of your time. You lead from the front - moving from architectural vision to working software, personally. If your preference is strategy with others implementing, this isn't the role. You architect by delivering.

Cross-Functional Influence at Scale: This work touches ~120+ engineers across multiple groups, plus Product and UX partners. You'll need to build alignment, communicate trade-offs clearly across all levels, and move a large org without steamrolling it.

Technical Mentorship & Multiplier: You elevate the engineers around you-  raising the bar on full-stack product thinking, AI-enabled development, and what it means to build software that customers actually use and love.

Product & Customer Obsession: You understand the pain of a CRM customer who needs software to flex to their workflow, not the other way around. You bring that perspective into every technical decision you make.

What You Bring

Full-Stack Product Engineering Depth: You've delivered meaningful impact on both sides-  backend systems and product-facing layers-  and you own end-to-end. You're not purely infrastructure, and you're not purely UI. You span both because the best product outcomes require it.

AI Shipped to Production: You've gone beyond experimentation. You've delivered AI-powered product features with real user impact-  ideally at the intersection of configurability, extensibility, or no-code/low-code tooling and AI capability.

A Product-First Mindset: You care deeply about the "why" behind the "what." You've built things people use every day, and you advocate for the customer experience in design reviews- even when it means rethinking the technical approach.

SaaS Product Background: You've operated inside a product-led SaaS company that moves fast and operates at scale. You understand the difference between building for enterprise customers and building for storefronts or one-off client engagements. (E-commerce, agency, and IT-cost-center experience tends not to translate to this environment.)

title: Principal Software Engineer, Release Engineering
description:
POS-32873

About the Team

HubSpot's Developer Acceleration group empowers over 2,000 engineers to build, test, and deploy their code at scale. The release engineering team owns the full delivery pipeline — from pull request to production — and is responsible for hundreds of thousands of builds per day, including tens of thousands of QA deployments. 

We're in the middle of a fundamental shift. Agentic AI is changing what release engineering can look like — from AI-powered QA agents that evaluate every deploy, to systems that can reason about risk, surface anomalies, and make autonomous decisions in the delivery pipeline. The team is actively building toward this future, and the opportunity for someone who can help shape it is significant.

The team owns and evolves some of the most critical foundational systems inside HubSpot's engineering organization, including build infrastructure, test orchestration, deployment pipelines, and the tooling that underpins incident management and production reliability. This is not a team focused on maintaining existing systems. It is an engineering organization responsible for rethinking how software gets shipped at scale — and what becomes possible when intelligent agents are embedded throughout that process.

About the Role

We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to help define the technical future of release engineering at HubSpot — at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems and agentic AI.

The role of AI in software delivery is no longer theoretical. We're actively deploying AI agents across our build, test, and deploy pipeline, and we're only at the beginning of understanding what's possible. This is a rare opportunity to work on infrastructure problems that very few engineers have encountered — at a scale that demands novel approaches — while helping to define what AI-native release engineering looks like in practice.

At HubSpot, Principal Engineers are expected to stay close to the code, lead high-impact initiatives end-to-end, and influence technical direction well beyond a single team. This role is for someone who can move between infrastructure architecture, agentic AI systems, and large-scale delivery pipeline design while remaining a hands-on builder throughout

Key Expectations

Own the future of HubSpot's release engineering platform

Shape the technical direction for the build, test, and deploy systems that underpin how HubSpot ships software.

Drive architectural decisions across pipeline design, test infrastructure, deployment orchestration, and developer ergonomics.

Help define what the next generation of HubSpot's delivery platform should look like — not just how to operate the current one.

Be a deeply hands-on, high-leverage builder

Write production code regularly and lead complex initiatives from idea to rollout.

Design and implement AI-powered QA agents that run on every deploy, reducing risk and increasing confidence in continuous delivery.

Turn ambiguous infrastructure problems into simple, scalable systems and clear technical direction.

Rethink testing and delivery infrastructure for a new era

Challenge 10-year-old assumptions about build systems and deployment pipelines given what's actually possible today.

Rethink testing infrastructure for a world where software behavior is increasingly non-deterministic.

Drive the roadmap toward 500+ deploys per minute, identifying and eliminating bottlenecks across the delivery pipeline.

Influence across the broader engineering org

Partner with engineering leaders to align release engineering direction with what HubSpot needs to build next.

Work horizontally across teams to guide technical tradeoffs, rationalize configuration and change management across concurrent teams, and raise the architectural bar for platform work.

Act as a multiplier through design reviews, technical mentoring, and principled decision-making on the most critical systems in the space.

What You Bring

Deep experience building and evolving large-scale distributed systems, particularly in CI/CD, build infrastructure, release engineering, or foundational backend platforms.

Strong architectural instincts with a bias toward simplicity, clarity, and long-term platform leverage — and a healthy skepticism toward complexity that isn't earned.

Experience operating at hyperscaler or platform-provider scale.

A track record of owning and delivering complex, cross-team technical initiatives with org-wide or company-level impact.

A hands-on mindset. You lead by building, debugging, reviewing, and shipping — not by staying removed from the systems you influence.

The ability to move into unfamiliar technical territory quickly, form strong opinions grounded in first principles, and help teams make better long-term decisions.

Why This Role Matters

HubSpot's engineering productivity depends on a delivery platform that is not only reliable, but fast, intelligent, and built for the scale we're operating at today — and the scale we're building toward. The Principal Software Engineer in Developer Acceleration will help determine how that platform evolves, how AI changes what's possible in software delivery, and how thousands of engineers across HubSpot ship better software, faster.

title: Principal Software Engineer - Revenue Hub
description:
POS-9034

About the Team

Revenue Hub is building the backbone for businesses to sell, bill, get paid, and manage revenue inside HubSpot. Our systems handle billions of dollars in transactions, so correctness, clarity, and predictability matter.

We're building a commerce platform where the data model, APIs, and flows are first-class. Reps, admins, and agents all work from the same foundation. The vision is a single, connected revenue flow: Contact to Deal to Quote to Order to Contract to Invoice to Payment to Reconciliation. When that flow is clean and trusted, revenue context becomes available across the whole business: marketing can attribute spend to real revenue, sales can forecast on actual billing behavior, and service teams can see renewal risk before it's too late.

About the Role

We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to help shape the technical future of Revenue Hub. This is a very hands-on role. You'll write code, dive into services, review tough designs, debug messy systems, and directly own the architecture behind CPQ, Billing, Payments, and Revenue OS. A big part of this role is defining how external developers and AI agents interact with those surfaces safely and predictably.

What You'll Do

Build a simple, consistent, extensible platform

Shape the technical roadmap across CPQ, Billing, and Payments with strong, opinionated patterns.

Define and evolve core domain models so pricing, products, contracts, invoices, and payments behave predictably in the UI, over the API, and inside agent-driven workflows.

Design the API and platform contracts that let developers, partners, and AI agents extend Revenue Hub without coupling to internals.

Create frameworks that make the platform easy to extend without adding complexity.

Be a deeply hands-on, high-leverage builder

Write code regularly. Lead design reviews and build high-impact systems end-to-end.

Own large multi-team initiatives that span CPQ, Billing, and Payments.

Take prototypes to production at scale.

Lead architectural direction

Set patterns for extensibility, contract boundaries, financial correctness, event-driven consistency, and how AI agents safely interact with commerce objects.

Push for simplicity where the domain wants to get complicated, and consistency where surfaces can drift.

description:
POS- 29555

About You:

You’re a highly technical, execution-driven program leader who thrives working alongside security engineers and product leaders to ship meaningful security improvements at scale. You bring structure to complex, fast-moving initiatives without slowing them down, and you earn trust with engineers and senior leaders alike by understanding the work deeply enough to drive it forward. You shape platform direction, influence executive decisions, and connect security program outcomes to long-term business impact. You’re comfortable operating autonomously in ambiguous environments, know how to navigate organizational complexity, and use AI as a genuine force multiplier in your daily work.

About Us:

The HubSpot Security team is dedicated to helping businesses grow better by safeguarding the systems and data that power our global CRM platform. With more than 125,000 customers in over 100 countries, HubSpot’s security posture is essential to our mission and a competitive differentiator.

As part of the Security Governance and Risk team, you’ll:

Partner closely with security engineering teams to drive the Security Product Line’s highest-priority initiatives from planning through delivery.

Operate at the intersection of security, engineering, and governance, keeping complex multi-team programs moving and unblocking what needs to get done.

Shape how the Security Governance group operates at scale, building the operating rhythms, frameworks, and tooling that let security teams do their best work.

Join a culture that values transparency, learning, and authenticity.

In this role you will…

Security Engineering Partnership (Core Focus)

Serve as an embedded TPM for security engineering teams, owning program execution for the Security Product Line’s most complex and strategically important initiatives.

Drive end-to-end delivery of large-scale security programs spanning detection and response, identity and access, infrastructure security, application security, and more.

Partner with security engineering leads and product managers to define roadmaps, sequence work, manage dependencies to keep initiatives on track.

Navigate ambiguity and organizational complexity independently, escalating the right things to the right people and clearing blockers before they become delays.Champion scalable processes and durable systems within the security organization, raising the operational bar across the product line.

Own portfolio-level KPIs, building reporting that connects program delivery to customer, reliability, and business outcomes.

Serve as a thought leader within the TPM function, sharing strategies,approaches, and AI enabled workflows that elevate how the whole team works.

SOX Compliance for UBB (Near-Term Priority)

In the near term, this role will focus on supporting SOX compliance for HubSpot’s Usage-Based Billing features. The goal is to build a streamlined, repeatable process for bringing UBB features into SOX compliance, at which point this role hands off to a more sustainable operating model and shifts fully into security engineering TPM support.

Partner with FinTech and FinOps program management to coordinate SOX compliance work across Engineering, Finance, and Security, keeping the program moving and stakeholders aligned.

Drive implementation of SOX-compliant technical controls, partnering closely with engineering teams to sequence the work, remove blockers, and get features across the line.

Ensure UBB features are integrated into the right SOX control frameworks and that engineering teams understand compliance requirements well enough to build compliantly from the start.

Build a repeatable, scalable playbook so new UBB features can be evaluated, instrumented, and brought into SOX compliance without starting from scratch each time.

AI-Powered Execution

Actively use AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) to accelerate program planning, documentation, risk analysis, and stakeholder communications.

Model AI-fluent working habits for the team, sharing workflows and prompting strategies that multiply output quality and speed.

Identify where AI materially changes how security engineering programs are planned, executed, or measured, and translate those opportunities into program strategy and investment priorities.

We are looking for people who have…

12+ years of technical program management experience, with a significant portion embedded with security or software engineering teams in a SaaS or cloud environment.

Deep enough technical fluency to earn credibility with security engineers, understand the work, and ask the right questions without needing to be a practitioner.

Experience partnering with senior security engineering leaders to shape platform direction, technical standards, and execution guardrails, and the ability to connect security program outcomes to long-term business leverage and security risk.

Hands-on experience leading security programs across domains such as detection and response, identity and access management, infrastructure security, application security, and more.

The ability to build durable operating systems: program structures, escalation paths, reporting cadences, and tooling that outlast individual initiatives.

Familiarity with compliance security frameworks and standards such as SOX, ISO 27001, NIST, SOC 2, or MITRE ATT&CK sufficient to navigate security conversations and program requirements.

Demonstrated AI fluency, with a habit of using AI tools to improve the quality, speed, and consistency of program management work. You don’t just know these tools exist; you use them daily and have strong opinions on how they fit into a TPM’s workflow.

Experience as a force multiplier for a TPM team, including developing methodologies, mentoring peers, and raising the bar on program quality.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical and operational topics for diverse audiences.

Hands-on experience working with security engineering teams on major platform or infrastructure security initiatives.

Familiarity with SaaS architecture and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP) at a depth that helps you understand security engineering trade-offs.

Certification(s) such as PMP, CISM, CISSP, or CISA.

Prior experience with Usage-Based Billing or revenue recognition controls in a SaaS context.

title: Revenue Operations Coordinator
description:
POS-33516

About the Role

SPOT — the Solutions Partner Operations Team — is the operational backbone of HubSpot's Solutions Partner Program. We're the team that makes sure partners get paid accurately and on time, that payment questions get resolved quickly, and that new program pilots have the operational infrastructure they need to land cleanly.

We're looking for a Revenue Operations Specialist who can handle the core commissions and payment workload with consistency and accuracy, and step into new pilots as the person who figures out what needs to happen operationally before anything goes live. This isn't a build-it-and-hand-it-off role — you'll own the processes you run and the programs you help stand up.

What You'll Do

Commissions Pipeline

Own your share of the commissions pipeline — processing partner payments accurately, on cadence, and without errors. You'll work through the full payment cycle, cross-checking data across systems, catching discrepancies before they become partner-facing issues, and keeping your queue current. Consistency and accuracy matter here more than speed; partners trust that their commissions are right, and you'll be part of keeping that trust.

Payment Inquiries & Partner Support

Serve as a point of contact for payment-related questions from partners and internal stakeholders. When a payment inquiry comes in, you'll own it — investigating the issue, coordinating with Finance where needed, communicating clearly with the partner or PDM, and closing it out. You won't pass questions along and wait; you'll drive them to resolution.

Manual Pilot Support

When SPOT takes on a new program pilot, there's almost always a manual operational layer that needs to be built before automation catches up. You'll be the person who owns that layer — mapping out every step, executing it accurately, flagging gaps as they surface, and helping document the process so it can be handed off or automated over time. You're comfortable with ambiguity and you know how to build structure where none exists yet.

Process & Documentation

Maintain clean, up-to-date process documentation for every workstream you own. When a process changes, your docs change with it — not after the fact. You'll also surface recurring errors or patterns to the team so we can fix root causes, not just individual tickets.

What We're Looking For

1–3 years in an operations, finance operations, or revenue operations role — experience with commissions or partner payments is a strong plus

High attention to detail and a low tolerance for errors — you double-check your work before it goes out

Ability to own a process end-to-end, not just execute individual tasks within it

Clear, professional communicator — partners and PDMs will be counting on you for accurate, timely responses

Comfortable working across systems — SNOW, Partner Admin, NetSuite, Xactly, or similar tools

Proactive about flagging issues and bringing a proposed resolution, not just a question

Comfortable stepping into new programs with incomplete information and building structure as you go

Who Thrives in This Role

This role suits someone who takes real satisfaction in doing operational work well — where accuracy, consistency, and follow-through aren't just expectations but personal standards. You'll thrive if you find commission operations genuinely interesting, if you're the kind of person who notices when something doesn't add up and won't let it go until it's resolved, and if you get energy from being the person others can count on to close things out. When a new pilot lands on the team, you're not waiting for a full playbook — you ask the right questions, figure out the steps, and get moving. You take ownership seriously and you communicate clearly, even when the answer isn't what someone wants to hear.

description:

Senior Business Systems Analyst, Partner Systems & Automation

About the Team

HubSpot's Partner Systems & Automation team builds the systems, automations, and integrations that power HubSpot's partner ecosystem — one of the most strategically important parts of the business, representing a significant share of HubSpot revenue. We work across HubSpot's internal CRM portals, Workato, ServiceNow, Snowflake, and a range of third-party systems, and we are actively expanding our use of AI-assisted workflows to move faster from problem identification to working solutions.

We identify problems, design solutions, build them, ship them, and own them. Our BSAs sit at the boundary between business operations and technical execution — close enough to the business to understand what matters, and technical enough to build it. We are looking for a Senior BSA who thinks like a builder, operates like an engineer, and communicates like a business partner.

In This Role, You'll Get To

Take ownership of complex, cross-functional automation and systems work across HubSpot's Solutions Partner program — one of the most mature and technically demanding parts of our partner ecosystem

Identify inefficiencies and root causes across partner operations workflows, then design, build, test, and ship solutions

Build and maintain integrations, automations, and data pipelines using Workato and HubSpot CRM, with SQL and REST APIs as standard tools of the trade

Prototype AI-assisted workflows and automation agents, bringing them from idea to working implementation and iterating based on real usage data

Scope work rigorously — define the problem, quantify the impact, propose the right-sized solution, and know when to prototype before committing to a full build

Partner with stakeholders across Partner Operations, Partner Product, Engineering, Finance, and Analytics to translate business problems into technical solutions

Push back constructively when a request does not justify the investment, and help stakeholders understand why

Operate across multiple partner program domains over time — Solutions Partners is your primary home, but this team is deliberately moving toward cross-domain capability and you will be part of that shift

Contribute to the team's technical standards and share what you learn, so useful discoveries by one person become capabilities for everyone

We Are Looking For Someone With

4+ years of hands-on experience in a role where you built and shipped production systems — business systems analyst, automation engineer, internal tools engineer, or similarly technical operations role

Technical fluency across the systems stack — SQL, REST APIs, Python, and JSON are standard tools for you; you use them to understand, diagnose, and extend systems

Hands-on experience with iPaaS tools (Workato, Zapier, Boomi, or similar) — building and maintaining multi-step automations and integrations across complex systems

Comfort with engineering hygiene for production systems — version control, incremental rollouts, and basic testing practices that make what you build safe to operate and easy for others to maintain.

Either shipped an AI-assisted feature or automation that real users used, or have a strong production track record and genuine interest in applying AI to operational workflows

Comfort working in ambiguous environments where the right problem is not always the stated problem — you ask the questions that reframe the work before you start building

Experience working across multiple stakeholder groups with different incentives and priorities, and the ability to align people without formal authority

Strong written and verbal communication — you can explain a complex system to a non-technical audience and a complex business problem to an engineer

A sense of ownership that extends past delivery — you define expected outcomes before you build, check them after you ship, and treat the systems you own as your ongoing responsibility

HubSpot's Legal team is extremely technology-forward. Attorneys who believe that AI and great systems can transform how legal work gets done. Our Legal Technology team exists at the center of that bet: we build the AI agents, manage the systems and integrate their operational infrastructure which lets our lawyers focus on high-value legal work instead of manual process.

Build integrations: design and develop workflow automations and integrations using Workato and similar iPaaS platforms, connecting legal systems to the broader HubSpot stack.

Strong hands-on technical skills: SaaS application configuration, API usage, system integration design, and workflow automation

Real experience building and deploying AI solutions in enterprise environments: AI agents, agentic workflows, LLM-powered tools, or similar

Experience with iPaaS platforms for building integrations and automations
